title: Moussaka
subtitle: Greek layered lamb and aubergine bake with béchamel
excerpt: Layers of sliced aubergine, spiced lamb mince, and a thick béchamel sauce, baked until golden and set. The great celebratory dish of Greek cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moussaka is found across the Middle East and Balkans but the Greek version — with its thick béchamel topping — is the form most widely known internationally. The recipe was standardised and elevated by the Greek chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the 1920s, who added the béchamel layer based on French cuisine. Earlier versions used yoghurt instead. The dish is a significant undertaking: the aubergine must be prepared separately, the lamb sauce cooked, and the béchamel made, before the dish is assembled and baked. It rewards the effort and improves after resting overnight in the fridge.

recipeTools.notes: For the lamb sauce and the béchamel.
A deep oven dish, about 30 x 22 cm, for the moussaka.

content.text: Salt the aubergine slices and leave for 20 minutes before frying: this draws out excess moisture and reduces the amount of oil they absorb. Pat completely dry before frying. The lamb sauce should be fairly dry before layering: excess liquid will make the moussaka soggy. The béchamel must be thick enough to hold its shape when spooned: it should be the consistency of a very thick custard. Rest the finished moussaka for at least 20 minutes before cutting so it holds its shape.

Salt the aubergine slices and leave for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry. Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.

Make the lamb sauce: cook the onion in a little oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon, and allspice. Stir for 1 minute. Add the lamb mince and brown over high heat, breaking up lumps. Add the tomato puree, red wine, and tinned tomatoes. Add the bay leaves and season. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and dry.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually add the warm milk, whisking constantly, until smooth and thick. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Remove from the heat and beat in the eggs and half the cheese. The sauce should be very thick.

Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Layer half the aubergine in the base of the dish. Add all the lamb sauce. Layer the remaining aubergine on top. Pour the béchamel evenly over everything. Scatter with the remaining cheese. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 20 minutes before cutting.
